case.title: Composition monitoring across two dairy streams
case.text: Our dairy process handles both a relatively clear whey stream and an opaque milk concentrate. We want a pilot for composition monitoring, using laboratory protein and fat results where those variables are relevant. We can compare different measurement interfaces before choosing the installation. What first measurement concepts and comparison experiment would make sense for these two streams?

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: Inline NIR Reflection is primarily used for opaque or highly concentrated dairy products, such as yogurt, butter, or whole milk concentrates.
refs.claim: Opaque or highly concentrated dairy products (yogurt, butter, milk concentrates) are measured in-line with NIR diffuse reflection.

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: In these high-OD scenarios, a UV-ATR (Attenuated Total Reflection) probe is used.
refs.claim: For high optical density liquids an ATR probe is used: the evanescent wave gives a path of a few micrometres, so black or highly scattering fluids can be measured without dilution.

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: it fails when the milk becomes too "thick" or fat-rich, as the light cannot penetrate the sample
refs.claim: Transmission fails once the product becomes thick or fat-rich; reflection works in highly scattering media but is less representative for clear liquids.

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: strong absorption in the mid-IR region limits the corresponding spectral method to the analysis of very thin samples (usually less than 50 μm), but it opens up the possibility of using attenuated total reflectance (ATR)
refs.claim: Mid-IR absorbs so strongly that only very thin layers (<50 µm) can be measured – in practice via ATR.

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: as the media becomes more opaque, turbid, or highly concentrated, the signal in a standard transmission setup becomes saturated because the light cannot penetrate the bulk of the sample
refs.claim: Opaque, turbid or highly concentrated media saturate a transmission setup because light cannot pass through the sample.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: ATR fiber probes (Fig.1) enable the analysis of liquids and solid elastic samples, such as biological tissue, using specialized probes utilizing high-transmission fiber optics in the Mid-IR region.
related.claim: Mid-IR ATR fiber probes analyse liquids and elastic solids such as biological tissue.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: NIR Transmission is the preferred method for transparent or semi-transparent liquids, such as skim milk, whey, or permeate.
related.claim: For transparent or semi-transparent liquids (skim milk, whey, permeate) NIR transmission is the preferred method.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: NIR spectroscopy, with its relatively large penetration depth (up to several millimetres) even into dense solid samples due to low absorption and strong scattering
related.claim: NIR penetrates several millimetres even into dense solids and powders because of low absorption and strong scattering.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: A multispectral fiber probe, e.g. one combining MIR-ATR and fluorescence techniques into a single fiber optic probe shaft allows for the simultaneous acquisition of complementary chemical information from the exact same measurement point
related.claim: Heterogeneous solids like tissue need a combined probe that measures both methods at exactly the same point.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: As the powder blend passes the probe tip, the system captures spectra at high speeds without interrupting the production flow.
related.claim: For powder blends (tablet press feed frame) NIR reflection and Raman probes measure the blend as it passes the probe tip.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: For highly transparent liquids with low optical density, UV-Transmission or Transflection probes are ideal
related.claim: Clear liquids with low optical density: transmission or transflection probes with a defined 1–10 mm path give high sensitivity for low concentrations.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: In some cases, a Transflection probe can already be a combined solution working well for low-fat and high-fat containing milk products.
related.claim: A transflection probe can sometimes cover both low-fat (clearer) and high-fat products with one interface.

related.docTitle: AFS Process Control Slides
related.quote: Spectra of API in hot polymer obtained with Diamond cone ATR probe coupled to iC10 FTIR (MTAC)
related.claim: API in hot polymer melt was measured with a diamond ATR probe.

related.docTitle: LED-based NIR Sensor for Kidney Tumour Diagnostics (2017)
related.quote: It is important that the NIR light penetrates into the sample by up to 3 mm
related.claim: NIR light penetrates up to about 3 mm into tissue – deeper than other suitable spectral regions.

related.docTitle: Combined MIR ATR and Fluorescence Fiber Probe (2021)
related.quote: The application of fiber optic probes can be moreover indispensable for the spectroscopic analysis of solid inhomogeneous samples
related.claim: Fiber probes are indispensable for local analysis of inhomogeneous solids (pharma and food products, soils, tissue).

related.docTitle: Combined MIR ATR and Fluorescence Fiber Probe (2021)
related.quote: Although ATR spectroscopy is not optimal for the analysis of solid objects, its application for the analysis of biological tissues by fiber-based probes is one of the most important exceptions.
related.claim: ATR is not optimal for solid objects; biological tissue is an important exception.

related.docTitle: Combined MIR ATR and Fluorescence Fiber Probe (2021)
related.quote: light used in fluorimetry can penetrate to the depth of a few millimeters into the tissue
related.claim: Fluorescence light reaches a few millimetres into tissue, while ATR samples only a few micrometres.

related.docTitle: Combined MIR ATR and Fluorescence Fiber Probe (2021)
related.quote: which is true for liquid or soft solid samples and their components, allowing a tight contact with the probe head
related.claim: ATR needs a tight contact with the probe head – true for liquids and soft solids.

related.docTitle: Combined MIR ATR and Fluorescence Fiber Probe (2021)
related.quote: The main focus of the proposed technology is on analyzing nonhomogeneous solid samples, because it enables simultaneous measurements at the same point on the sample surface.
related.claim: The combined probe targets inhomogeneous solids because both methods measure at the same point.

decisions.reasoning: Not stated outright. The closest passage is “Our dairy process handles both a relatively clear whey stream and an opaque milk concentrate” [E], which suggests Opaque liquid. This matches the AFS material [1, 2, 3]: opaque or highly concentrated dairy products (yogurt, butter, milk concentrates) are measured in-line with NIR diffuse reflection. Note [4, 5]: mid-IR absorbs so strongly that only very thin layers (<50 µm) can be measured – in practice via ATR. Please confirm.
decisions.enquiryQuote: Our dairy process handles both a relatively clear whey stream and an opaque milk concentrate.

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: Experimentally, the probe is flush-mounted into a pipe or vat to interact directly with the flowing medium.
refs.claim: For dairy, the reflection probe is flush-mounted into a pipe or vat in contact with the flowing product.

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: Immersible fiber optic probes operating in various spectral regions from UV to mid-IR are increasingly being used for measuring liquid and soft or powdered solid samples.
refs.claim: Immersible probes from UV to mid-IR measure liquids, soft and powdered solids in situ.

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: Probe-based analysis is gaining widespread use in online analysis, such as in-line, in-process (chemical, biotechnological, natural) environments, as well as in-situ measurements, such as for field testing or for spectral diagnostics during surgery.
refs.claim: Probe-based analysis is used in-line and in-process, and in situ for field tests or during surgery.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: It allows for in-process analysis, i.e., directly in the process flow or reactor without sampling, eliminating delays and the risk of sample contamination.
related.claim: In-process measurement works directly in the flow or reactor without sampling – no delay and no contamination risk.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: Different absorption coefficients of light in NIR, Mid-IR, and Raman spectroscopy, as well as the depth of its penetration into a given dense medium (solid, liquid, or powder) also requires different measurement interfaces and techniques, such as various fiber optic probes: ATR, Transmission, Transflexion, Reflection, etc.
related.claim: Penetration depth differs between NIR, mid-IR and Raman, so each needs its own interface (ATR, transmission, transflection, reflection).

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: Near-IR vibrational spectroscopy (NIR) is the most common online analysis method performed using fiber optic probes.
related.claim: NIR is the most common method for online analysis with fiber probes.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: high light scattering by solid and dispersed samples, which enables measurements using diffuse reflectance, including measurements without direct contact with the sample, at a distance
related.claim: Because solids and dispersions scatter NIR light strongly, diffuse reflectance can measure without contact, at a distance.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: The experimental procedure involves the direct contact of the probe tip with the tissue during an operation, such as for kidney, colon, or rectal cancer.
related.claim: For tissue diagnostics the probe tip is brought into direct contact with the tissue during the operation.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: The use of fiber optics is critical here, as it allows the sensitive spectrometers to be located safely away from the vibration and dust of the manufacturing floor.
related.claim: Fiber optics let the spectrometer stay away from vibration and dust while the probe sits in the process.

related.docTitle: AFS Process Control Slides
related.quote: Robust 100-300m cables made with Silica fibers of low OH-content (<0.1ppm OH) enable remote industrial process-control
related.claim: Silica fiber cables of 100–300 m allow a remote analyzer – for the Vis-NIR range.

related.docTitle: AFS Process Control Slides
related.quote: PIR-fiber transmission range 3-16μm is in the perfect match with Black Body Spectral Radiance at 0-100°C and Finger-Print Region of Molecular Vibrations
related.claim: Mid-IR needs polycrystalline (PIR) fibers, which transmit 3–16 µm.

related.docTitle: AFS Process Control Slides
related.quote: measurement of water content in petroleum ATR-Probes with ATR-tips from ZrO 2 (& Diamond, etc.) sealed in PEEK-shaft
related.claim: Water in petroleum is measured with sealed ATR probes (ZrO2 or diamond tip in a PEEK shaft).

related.docTitle: AFS Process Control Slides
related.quote: NIR-Reflex & MIR-ATR-spectroscopy to control polymer extrusion in-line
related.claim: Polymer extrusion is controlled in-line with NIR reflection and MIR ATR probes.

related.docTitle: LED-based NIR Sensor for Kidney Tumour Diagnostics (2017)
related.quote: Another important advantage of the NIR diagnostics of tissue tumors, compared to traditional methods, is the measurement flexibility due to the application of fiber-based light guides and probes, which is necessary under clinical conditions (e.g., during a surgery).
related.claim: Fiber-based probes give the flexibility needed under clinical conditions, e.g. during surgery.

related.docTitle: LED-based NIR Sensor for Kidney Tumour Diagnostics (2017)
related.quote: In the latter case, therefore, the data was acquired at a distance of 3–4 mm above the tissue surface.
related.claim: In the improved prototype, the reflectance data were acquired 3–4 mm above the tissue surface (probe tip touching).

related.docTitle: Combined MIR ATR and Fluorescence Fiber Probe (2021)
related.quote: Fiber optics and probes on its basis enable sampling-free measurements in situ, thereby essentially expanding the scope of optical analysis compared to the traditional lab spectroscopy.
related.claim: Fiber probes enable sampling-free measurements in situ.

decisions.reasoning: The customer does not state this. The most likely value is In-process probe. This matches the AFS material [1, 2, 3]: for dairy, the reflection probe is flush-mounted into a pipe or vat in contact with the flowing product. Please confirm.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: allows the use of ordinary glass for optics, as well as standard lamps as light sources, making it ideal for online applications, including remote measurements via fiber optic probes
related.claim: NIR works with ordinary glass optics and standard lamps – simple hardware, well suited to remote fiber measurements.

related.docTitle: AFS Process Control Slides
related.quote: Robust 100-300m cables made with Silica fibers of low OH-content (<0.1ppm OH) enable remote industrial process-control
related.claim: Silica fiber cables of 100–300 m allow a remote analyzer – for the Vis-NIR range.

related.docTitle: AFS Process Control Slides
related.quote: PIR-fiber transmission range 3-16μm is in the perfect match with Black Body Spectral Radiance at 0-100°C and Finger-Print Region of Molecular Vibrations
related.claim: Mid-IR needs polycrystalline (PIR) fibers, which transmit 3–16 µm.

decisions.missing: Which fiber link connects analyzer and probe (fiber type, length), and could an IR fiber be used if mid-IR is the best method?
decisions.reasoning: Neither the enquiry nor the AFS material decides this. Ask the customer: Which fiber link connects analyzer and probe (fiber type, length), and could an IR fiber be used if mid-IR is the best method?

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: Data processing may involve converting the reflectance values to absorbance and applying Multiplicative Scatter Correction (MSC) or Standard Normal Variate (SNV) transformations to remove physical interference caused by the scattering nature of the milk particles before using Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression to quantify fat and protein.
refs.claim: Fat and protein in milk are quantified from NIR reflection spectra after scatter correction with PLS regression.

refs.quote: Comparison of spectral data for customer process enables to select the best process-control solution
refs.claim: AFS compares the spectral data of the customer's process across methods before choosing the process-control solution.

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: Raman spectroscopy can be used in the same reactor to provide a "molecular fingerprint" for direct detection of specific metabolites like glucose, acetate, or lactate.
refs.claim: Specific metabolites (glucose, acetate, lactate) are detected with Raman; it suits aqueous media because water absorbs weakly.

refs.docTitle: Combined MIR ATR and Fluorescence Fiber Probe (2021)
refs.quote: Of course, it is limited to the samples containing at least one fluorescent component that often has a biological or natural origin.
refs.claim: The MIR + fluorescence probe only applies to samples with at least one fluorescent component.

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: the strong overlap of spectral signals in UV spectra complicates the analysis of real samples and makes the use of chemometric algorithms a necessary component of qualitative mixture analysis methods
refs.claim: UV spectra of mixtures overlap strongly; quantification needs chemometrics (low selectivity).

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: However, most chemicals do not exhibit this property.
related.claim: Fluorimetry only works for substances that fluoresce – most chemicals do not.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: The combination of fluorescence and IR spectroscopy also proved necessary for classifying biological tissues.
related.claim: Classifying biological tissues required combining fluorescence and IR.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: These models automatically categorize the tissue as "normal" or "malignant," providing instant diagnostic results that serve as a "spectral biopsy".
related.claim: Tissue diagnostics is a classification task (normal vs malignant) solved with PCA / PLS-DA models.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: The combination of these techniques is particularly effective because it captures complementary chemical information: NIR detects hydrogen bonds and asymmetric polar groups, while Raman provides information on the molecular backbone and symmetrical non-polar groups.
related.claim: API content in powder blends: NIR and Raman give complementary chemical information.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: UV/Vis spectroscopy can be deployed as a low- cost, robust tool for real-time biomass monitoring, as cell suspension turbidity correlates well with cell density.
related.claim: Biomass can be followed with low-cost UV/Vis, because turbidity correlates with cell density.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: Fluorescence spectroscopy can be used for high- sensitivity detection (down to the nM-μM range) of critical cofactors and amino acids like NADH, tryptophan, and riboflavin.
related.claim: Fluorescence detects named fluorophores (NADH, tryptophan, riboflavin) at nM–µM levels.

related.docTitle: LED-based NIR Sensor for Kidney Tumour Diagnostics (2017)
related.quote: Diffuse reflectance near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy is one of the most promising methods for optical tissue analysis.
related.claim: Diffuse reflectance NIR is a promising method for distinguishing tissue types (tumour vs normal).

related.docTitle: LED-based NIR Sensor for Kidney Tumour Diagnostics (2017)
related.quote: It is common practice to use ex vivo samples at the early research stages, as in the present proof-of-concept study.
related.claim: The study used ex vivo samples at an early research stage; in vivo spectra can differ.

related.docTitle: LED-based NIR Sensor for Kidney Tumour Diagnostics (2017)
related.quote: The practicable diagnostic model should be built at a later stage of the method development, using a large representative set of patients, and should then be permanently updated with new data.
related.claim: A usable diagnostic model needs a large representative patient set – beyond the scope of the study.

related.docTitle: LED-based NIR Sensor for Kidney Tumour Diagnostics (2017)
related.quote: This study provides a proof-of-concept demonstration of the LED-based sensor for tumor discrimination.
related.claim: The LED sensor is only a proof of concept for tumour discrimination; further studies are needed.

related.docTitle: Combined MIR ATR and Fluorescence Fiber Probe (2021)
related.quote: However, none of the individual techniques was sufficient to completely separate the three sample classes on the PCA score plots
related.claim: No single method separated the three tissue classes; the combined IR + fluorescence data did.

decisions.reasoning: The customer writes “We want a pilot for composition monitoring, using laboratory protein and fat results where those variables are relevant” [E] – that is Chemical composition. The AFS material agrees [1, 2, 3]: fat and protein in milk are quantified from NIR reflection spectra after scatter correction with PLS regression. Note [4, 5]: the MIR + fluorescence probe only applies to samples with at least one fluorescent component.
decisions.enquiryQuote: We want a pilot for composition monitoring, using laboratory protein and fat results where those variables are relevant.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: Morphological factors, such as sample inhomogeneity (e.g., biological tissue) or process turbulence, must also be considered when selecting a measurement technique.
related.claim: Sample inhomogeneity and process turbulence must be considered when choosing the measurement technique.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: Situations are also possible where problems of inhomogeneity and rapid changes in the sample coexist. In these cases, the use of multispectral probes becomes essential.
related.claim: Where inhomogeneity and rapid changes coexist, multispectral probes become essential.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: Because the light does not penetrate deeply, the method is sensitive to the surface characteristics and fat globule size.
related.claim: Reflection is sensitive to surface properties and fat globule size – texture changes affect the signal.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: By maintaining both, a lab can calibrate models for every stage of production - from raw milk intake to final evaporation - ensuring that no matter how the physical state of the milk changes during processing, the inline monitoring remains accurate and robust.
related.claim: When the physical state changes along the process, calibrations for several interfaces keep the measurement robust.

related.docTitle: LED-based NIR Sensor for Kidney Tumour Diagnostics (2017)
related.quote: The main disadvantage of the LED-based sensor in its present form is a very high measurement variance in cancer tissue samples (Figure 9).
related.claim: Cancer tissue showed very high measurement variance – the main weakness of the sensor.

related.docTitle: Combined MIR ATR and Fluorescence Fiber Probe (2021)
related.quote: Low measurement reproducibility of the fat samples (broad standard deviation in Figure 2a) is explained by higher inhomogeneity of this tissue type
related.claim: Inhomogeneous tissue (fat) gave low measurement reproducibility.

decisions.missing: Do turbidity, optical density, texture or bubbles of the sample change during the process, and over what range?
decisions.reasoning: Neither the enquiry nor the AFS material decides this. Ask the customer: Do turbidity, optical density, texture or bubbles of the sample change during the process, and over what range?

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: NIR spectroscopy is effective for tracking major components like glucose or glycerol in the millimolar range but may lack the sensitivity to detect trace compounds below 0.1 percent.
related.claim: NIR tracks major components (mM range) but may miss trace compounds below 0.1 %.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: Fluorescence spectroscopy can be used for high- sensitivity detection (down to the nM-μM range) of critical cofactors and amino acids like NADH, tryptophan, and riboflavin.
related.claim: Trace-level fluorophores (nM–µM) need fluorescence spectroscopy.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: they pass light through a defined path length (typically 1 mm to 10 mm), allowing for high sensitivity and accurate quantification of low- concentration analytes
related.claim: Transmission with a defined path allows accurate quantification of low-concentration analytes in clear liquids.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: This technique generally offers higher accuracy for low-concentration components because the light interacts with the entire volume of the sampled cross-section, providing a more representative chemical signature.
related.claim: Transmission through the whole cross-section gives higher accuracy for low-concentration components.

decisions.missing: In what concentration range is the target present, and what change must be detected?
decisions.reasoning: Neither the enquiry nor the AFS material decides this. Ask the customer: In what concentration range is the target present, and what change must be detected?

We want a pilot for composition monitoring, using laboratory protein and fat results where those variables are relevant. We can compare different measurement interfaces before choosing the installation. What first measurement concepts and comparison experiment would make sense for these two streams?

steps.customerQuote: Our dairy process handles both a relatively clear whey stream and an opaque milk concentrate.
steps.question: What is the physical state and optical appearance of the sample at the measurement point (powder, clear / turbid / opaque liquid, paste or melt, solid)?

steps.title: Measurement interface
steps.question: Should the measurement be in-line with a probe, contact-free at a distance, or on laboratory samples?

steps.title: Usable spectral range

steps.customerQuote: We want a pilot for composition monitoring, using laboratory protein and fat results where those variables are relevant.

recommendation.text: Worth testing if the samples are liquid, paste or soft and an in‑line probe can be installed, and a mid‑IR‑compatible fiber link is available; ATR works with highly scattering or opaque liquids without dilution [E15][E16][E17].

Worth testing if the samples can be presented to an in‑line probe (liquid, powder or solid) and the process tolerates the probe geometry; Raman gives high chemical selectivity for protein and fat [E18][E16][E17].

Worth testing in a laboratory feasibility set‑up if the samples are liquid and a thin path (<50 µm) can be prepared; useful for initial correlation studies before in‑line deployment [E19][E16][E17][E20].

report.measurementConcept: Use a flush‑mounted reflection probe for the opaque milk concentrate and a transmission or ATR arrangement for the clearer whey; both probes can be linked to the analyser via appropriate fiber (UV/Vis/NIR or MIR) and positioned in the pipe or a bench‑top flow cell [E1][E3][E6].
report.spectralRange: Mid‑IR nominal 4000–400 cm⁻¹ (2.5–25 µm) for ATR and cuvette methods; visible/short‑wave NIR 400–1100 nm for Raman. The exact fiber transmission capability must be verified for the chosen range [E15][E18].
risks: Sample may be a powder, melt or rigid solid, making ATR or Raman probe unsuitable [E17]
High turbidity or opacity could saturate transmission setups, reducing signal quality [E5][E3]
Mid‑IR fibers may not be available or long enough for the plant layout
Probe fouling or coating by milk fat could degrade performance over time
feasibilityPlan: Collect representative whey and milk‑concentrate samples at the intended measurement point.
Perform laboratory MIR cuvette measurements on each sample and correlate spectra with the known protein and fat values.
Set up a bench‑top flow cell with an ATR probe, measure both streams under flow, and record spectra.
Acquire Raman spectra with a probe compatible with liquids and powders on the same samples.
Analyse the data with chemometric models (e.g., PLS) and compare prediction errors and robustness across the three techniques.
report.decisionBasis: Proceed to full in‑line deployment if a method achieves a strong correlation (e.g., R² > 0.9) with laboratory protein and fat results, meets the required detection change, and demonstrates acceptable robustness to fouling and optical variability; otherwise reject or revisit the measurement concept.

evidence.text: Opaque or highly concentrated dairy products (yogurt, butter, milk concentrates) are measured in-line with NIR diffuse reflection.
evidence.quote: Inline NIR Reflection is primarily used for opaque or highly concentrated dairy products, such as yogurt, butter, or whole milk concentrates.

evidence.text: For high optical density liquids an ATR probe is used: the evanescent wave gives a path of a few micrometres, so black or highly scattering fluids can be measured without dilution.
evidence.quote: In these high-OD scenarios, a UV-ATR (Attenuated Total Reflection) probe is used.

evidence.text: Transmission fails once the product becomes thick or fat-rich; reflection works in highly scattering media but is less representative for clear liquids.
evidence.quote: it fails when the milk becomes too "thick" or fat-rich, as the light cannot penetrate the sample

evidence.text: Mid-IR absorbs so strongly that only very thin layers (<50 µm) can be measured – in practice via ATR.
evidence.quote: strong absorption in the mid-IR region limits the corresponding spectral method to the analysis of very thin samples (usually less than 50 μm), but it opens up the possibility of using attenuated total reflectance (ATR)

evidence.text: Opaque, turbid or highly concentrated media saturate a transmission setup because light cannot pass through the sample.
evidence.quote: as the media becomes more opaque, turbid, or highly concentrated, the signal in a standard transmission setup becomes saturated because the light cannot penetrate the bulk of the sample

evidence.text: For dairy, the reflection probe is flush-mounted into a pipe or vat in contact with the flowing product.
evidence.quote: Experimentally, the probe is flush-mounted into a pipe or vat to interact directly with the flowing medium.

evidence.text: Immersible probes from UV to mid-IR measure liquids, soft and powdered solids in situ.
evidence.quote: Immersible fiber optic probes operating in various spectral regions from UV to mid-IR are increasingly being used for measuring liquid and soft or powdered solid samples.

evidence.text: Probe-based analysis is used in-line and in-process, and in situ for field tests or during surgery.
evidence.quote: Probe-based analysis is gaining widespread use in online analysis, such as in-line, in-process (chemical, biotechnological, natural) environments, as well as in-situ measurements, such as for field testing or for spectral diagnostics during surgery.
